title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 129 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 609–611 (Night 129, continuing directly from nights-128), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 129 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between. Tāj al-Mulūk, on fire at the mention of the lady Dunyā, asks ʿAzīz how he came to see her, and ʿAzīz tells of an old gardener who let him into her garden below the palace, where he glimpsed her for an hour and knew that he, a merchant unmanned, could never come near her. Tāj al-Mulūk takes ʿAzīz home to his father's city and falls into a lovesick decline, in love with a woman he has only heard of; his father finds him wasted and tearful, hears the whole story, and tells him to put her out of his mind. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ وَالْعِشْرُونَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿatu wa-al-ʿishrūna baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the ninth and the twenty after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and twenty-ninth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ قَالَ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-wazīra dandāna qāla li-ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the vizier Dandān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the vizier Dandān told Ḍawʾ al-Makān:

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ قِصَّةَ الشَّابِّ تَعَجَّبَ غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ وَانْطَلَقَتْ فِي فُؤَادِهِ النِّيرَانُ لَمَّا سَمِعَ بِجَمَالِ السَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا وَعَرَفَ أَنَّهَا هِيَ الَّتِي تَرْقُمُ الْغِزْلَانَ وَزَادَ بِهِ الْوَجْدُ وَالْهُيَامُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa tāju al-mulūki qiṣṣata al-shābbi taʿajjaba ghāyata al-ʿajabi wa-inṭalaqat fī fuʾādihi al-nīrānu lammā samiʿa bi-jamāli al-sayyidati dunyā wa-ʿarafa annahā hiya allatī tarqumu al-ghizlāna wa-zāda bihi al-wajdu wa-al-huyāmu
sentences.l: And when Tāj al-Mulūk heard the story of the young-man, he wondered the utmost of wonder, and the fires were-let-loose in his heart when he heard of the beauty of the lady Dunyā and knew that she, she was the-one-who embroiders the gazelles; and passion and love-madness increased upon him.
sentences.i: When Tāj al-Mulūk heard the young man’s story he was utterly amazed, and fire broke out in his heart as he heard of the lady Dunyā’s beauty and learned that she was the one who worked the gazelles; and his passion and the madness of love grew upon him.
sentences.n: The night again goes back over the last one’s ending before moving on. samiʿa bi-, “heard of”: the bi- marks what one hears about. tarqumu, “embroiders, figures”: raqama is to mark or work a pattern into cloth, the word for the gazelles stitched on the cloth ʿAzīz carries. zāda bihi, “increased with him”, i.e. grew upon him. wajd and huyām are two words for the passion of love, the second its distracted, wandering form.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِلشَّابِّ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ جَرَى لَكَ شَيْءٌ مَاجَرَى لِأَحَدٍ غَيْرِكَ مِثْلُهُ وَلَكِنْ لَكَ عُمْرٌ تَقْضِيهِ وَقَصْدِي أَنْ أَسْأَلَكَ عَنْ شَيْءٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla li-al-shābbi wa-allāhi la-qad jarā laka shayʾun mā jarā li-aḥadin ghayrika mithluhu wa-lākin laka ʿumrun taqḍīhi wa-qaṣdī an asʾalaka ʿan shayʾin
sentences.l: And he said to the young-man: By God, there has happened to you a thing the like of which has not happened to anyone other than you; but you have a life-span that you will live out. And my purpose is that I ask you about a thing.
sentences.i: He said to the young man: “By God, there has befallen you something such as has befallen no one else; but you have a lifetime still to live out. Now I would ask you about something.”
sentences.n: The print has وتصدي, a misprint for وقصدي, “and my purpose”, corrected here. laka ʿumrun taqḍīhi, “you have a life-span you will spend”: a consolation — what was fated has happened, and the rest of his days are still his. mā jarā, “has not happened”, run together in the print.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عَزِيزٌ وَمَاهُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿazīzun wa-mā huwa
sentences.l: And ʿAzīz said: And what is it?
sentences.i: “And what is it?” said ʿAzīz.
sentences.n: wa-mā huwa, run together in the print.

sentences.t: قَالَ تَحْكِي لِي كَيْفَ رَأَيْتَ تِلْكَ الصَّبِيَّةَ الَّتِي عَمِلَتْ هَذَا الْغَزَالَ
sentences.tr: qāla taḥkī lī kayfa raʾayta tilka al-ṣabiyyata allatī ʿamilat hādhā al-ghazāla
sentences.l: He said: You tell me how you saw that girl who made this gazelle.
sentences.i: He said: “Tell me how you came to see the girl who made this gazelle.”
sentences.n: taḥkī lī, “you tell me”: the plain imperfect used as a request, as in spoken Arabic, where Classical would have the imperative iḥki.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا مَوْلَايَ إِنِّي أَتَيْتُهَا بِحِيلَةٍ وَهُوَ أَنِّي لَمَّا دَخَلْتُ مَعَ الْقَافِلَةِ إِلَى بَلَدِهَا كُنْتُ أَخْرُجُ وَأَدُورُ فِى الْبَسَاتِينِ وَهِيَ كَثِيرَةُ الْأَشْجَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā mawlāya innī ataytuhā bi-ḥīlatin wa-huwa annī lammā dakhaltu maʿa al-qāfilati ilā baladihā kuntu akhruju wa-adūru fī al-basātīni wa-hiya kathīratu al-ashjāri
sentences.l: And he said: O my master, I came to her by a stratagem, and it is that I, when I entered with the caravan into her country, used to go out and go round in the gardens — and they are many of trees.
sentences.i: He said: “My lord, I reached her by a ruse. When I came into her country with the caravan, I used to go out and wander about the gardens, which are thick with trees.
sentences.n: atā bi-, “come by means of”: here bi- is the means, “by a stratagem”. wa-huwa annī, “and it is that I …”: the masculine huwa refers loosely to the whole matter rather than to the feminine ḥīla, a common loose agreement in the text. kuntu akhruju, “I used to go out”: kāna with the imperfect marks a repeated habit.

sentences.t: وَحَارِسُ تِلْكَ الْبَسَاتِينِ شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ طَاعِنٌ فِى السِّنِّ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥārisu tilka al-basātīni shaykhun kabīrun ṭāʿinun fī al-sinni
sentences.l: And the guard of those gardens was an old-man, great, thrust-forward in age.
sentences.i: The keeper of those gardens was a very old man, far gone in years.
sentences.n: ṭāʿinun fī al-sinni, “thrust forward in age”: the set phrase for great age; ṭaʿana is to pierce or push on.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ يَا شَيْخُ لِمَنْ هَذَا الْبُسْتَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu yā shaykhu li-man hādhā al-bustānu
sentences.l: And I said to him: O old-man, to whom is this garden?
sentences.i: I said to him: ‘Old man, whose garden is this?’

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي هُوَ لِابْنَةِ الْمَلِكِ السِّتِّ دُنْيَا وَنَحْنُ تَحْتَ قَصْرِهَا فَإِذَا أَرَادَتْ أَنْ تَتَفَرَّجَ تَفْتَحُ بَابَ السِّرِّ وَتَتَفَرَّجُ فِى الْبُسْتَانِ وَتَشُمُّ رَوَائِحَ الْأَزْهَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī huwa li-ibnati al-maliki al-sitti dunyā wa-naḥnu taḥta qaṣrihā fa-idhā arādat an tatafarraja taftaḥu bāba al-sirri wa-tatafarraju fī al-bustāni wa-tashummu rawāʾiḥa al-azhāri
sentences.l: And he said to me: It is for the daughter of the king, the lady Dunyā; and we are beneath her palace, and when she wants to take-her-pleasure she opens the door of the secret and takes-her-pleasure in the garden and smells the scents of the flowers.
sentences.i: He said to me: ‘It belongs to the king’s daughter, the lady Dunyā. We are just below her palace, and when she wants to take the air she opens the private door and strolls in the garden and breathes the scent of the flowers.’
sentences.n: li-ibnati, “to the daughter”: the li- of belonging, “it is hers”. tafarraja, “to look about for pleasure, to take one’s ease”, a favourite word of the later Nights. bāb al-sirr, “the door of the secret”, a private or hidden door; the print points the shadda in al-sirr, as it does in tashummu.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ أَنْعِمْ عَلَيَّ بِأَنْ أَقْعُدَ فِي هَذَا الْبُسْتَانِ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَ وَتَمُرَّ لَعَلِّي أَحْظَى مِنْهَا بِنَظْرَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu anʿim ʿalayya bi-an aqʿuda fī hādhā al-bustāni ḥattā taʾtiya wa-tamurra laʿallī aḥẓā minhā bi-naẓratin
sentences.l: And I said to him: Bestow-favour on me with that I sit in this garden until she comes and passes, perhaps I may win from her a glance.
sentences.i: I said to him: ‘Do me the kindness of letting me sit in this garden until she comes by; perhaps I may be granted a glimpse of her.’
sentences.n: anʿim ʿalayya bi-, “do me the favour of”: the verb takes bi- for the favour granted. aḥẓā bi-, “obtain, be favoured with”: here bi- marks the thing won, “a glance”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ لَابَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu lā baʾsa bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And the old-man said: No harm in that.
sentences.i: ‘There is no harm in that,’ said the old man.
sentences.n: lā baʾsa bi-, “there is no harm in”: bi- marks the thing judged harmless; run together, and without hamza, in the print.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَالَ لِي ذَلِكَ أَعْطَيْتُهُ بَعْضَ دَرَاهِمَ وَقُلْتُ لَهُ اشْتَرِ لَنَا شَيْأً نَأْكُلُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qāla lī dhālika aʿṭaytuhu baʿḍa darāhima wa-qultu lahu ishtari lanā shayʾan naʾkuluhu
sentences.l: And when he said that to me, I gave him some dirhams and said to him: Buy for us a thing we may eat it.
sentences.i: When he said that, I gave him a few dirhams and told him: ‘Buy us something to eat.’
sentences.n: shayʾan, “something”, spelled شيأ in the print, with the hamza written on the alif of the accusative ending, as the print spells it throughout. naʾkuluhu, “we eat it”: an unmarked relative clause after an indefinite noun, “a thing we may eat”.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَهُمْ وَهُوَ فَرْحَانُ وَفَتَحَ الْبَابَ وَدَخَلَ وَأَدْخَلَنِي مَعَهُ وَسِرْنَا وَمَا زِلْنَا سَائِرِينَ إِلَى أَنْ أَتَيْنَا إِلَى مَكَانٍ لَطِيفٍ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhahum wa-huwa farḥānu wa-fataḥa al-bāba wa-dakhala wa-adkhalanī maʿahu wa-sirnā wa-mā zilnā sāʾirīna ilā an ataynā ilā makānin laṭīfin
sentences.l: And he took them, he being glad, and opened the door and entered and made-me-enter with him; and we went, and we did not cease going until we came to a pleasant place.
sentences.i: He took them gladly, opened the door, went in and brought me in with him; and we walked on and on until we came to a pleasant spot.
sentences.n: akhadhahum, “he took them”: the dirhams, referred to with the masculine plural pronoun used for people, a looseness of the spoken language. farḥān, “glad”: a form beside fariḥ, much favoured in later and spoken Arabic. mā zilnā sāʾirīna, “we did not cease going”: the storyteller’s way of saying “we went on and on”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِي اجْلِسْ هُنَا إِلَى أَنْ أَذْهَبَ وَأَعُودَ إِلَيْكَ بَعْدَ أَنْ أُحْضِرَ لِي شَيْأً مِنَ الْفَوَاكِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lī ijlis hunā ilā an adhhaba wa-aʿūda ilayka baʿda an uḥḍira lī shayʾan mina al-fawākihi
sentences.l: And he said to me: Sit here until I go and return to you after I bring for me a thing of the fruits.
sentences.i: And he said to me: ‘Sit here until I have gone and come back to you, once I have fetched some fruit.’
sentences.n: uḥḍira lī, “that I bring for me”: the lī is the old man’s, as a speaker says “get myself something”; the fruit is for them both.

sentences.t: وَتَرَكَنِي وَمَضَى وَغَابَ سَاعَةً وَرَجَعَ وَمَعَهُ خَرُوفٌ مَشْوِيٌّ فَأَكَلْنَا حَتَّى اكْتَفَيْنَا وَقَلْبِي مُشْتَاقٌ إِلَى رُؤْيَةِ الصَّبِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-tarakanī wa-maḍā wa-ghāba sāʿatan wa-rajaʿa wa-maʿahu kharūfun mashwiyyun fa-akalnā ḥattā iktafaynā wa-qalbī mushtāqun ilā ruʾyati al-ṣabiyyati
sentences.l: And he left me and went off, and was absent an hour, and returned, and with him a roasted lamb; and we ate until we had enough, and my heart longing for the sight of the girl.
sentences.i: He left me and went off, was gone an hour, and came back with a roast lamb. We ate our fill, and all the while my heart longed for the sight of the girl.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ جَالِسَانِ وَإِذَا بِالْبَابِ قَدِ انْفَتَحَ فَقَالَ لِي قُمِ اخْتَفِ فَقُمْتُ وَاخْتَفَيْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā naḥnu jālisāni wa-idhā bi-al-bābi qadi infataḥa fa-qāla lī qumi ikhtafi fa-qumtu wa-ikhtafaytu
sentences.l: And while we two were sitting, and behold, the door had opened; and he said to me: Rise, hide! And I rose and hid.
sentences.i: As the two of us sat there, suddenly the door opened. ‘Up, hide yourself!’ he said, and I got up and hid.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-al-bābi, “and behold, the door”: after idhā of surprise, bi- only marks what appears. jālisāni, “sitting”, in the dual: the two of them.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِطَوَاشِي أَسْوَدَ أَخْرَجَ رَأْسَهُ مِنْ بَابِ الرِّيحِ وَقَالَ يَا شَيْخُ هَلْ عِنْدَكَ أَحَدٌ فَقَالَ لَا
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-ṭawāshī aswada akhraja raʾsahu min bābi al-rīḥi wa-qāla yā shaykhu hal ʿindaka aḥadun fa-qāla lā
sentences.l: And behold, a black eunuch put-out his head from the door of the wind and said: O old-man, is there with you anyone? And he said: No.
sentences.i: And there was a black eunuch, putting his head out of the wind-door. ‘Old man,’ he said, ‘is anyone with you?’ ‘No,’ he said.
sentences.n: ṭawāshī, “eunuch”, a Turkish word common in the later Nights; the palace women are served by eunuchs. bāb al-rīḥ, “the door of the wind”: apparently a small opening or hatch letting air into the palace wall; the exact sense is not certain.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَغْلِقْ بَابَ الْبُسْتَانِ فَأَغْلَقَ الشَّيْخُ بَابَ الْبُسْتَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu aghliq bāba al-bustāni fa-aghlaqa al-shaykhu bāba al-bustāni
sentences.l: And he said to him: Shut the door of the garden. And the old-man shut the door of the garden.
sentences.i: ‘Lock the garden gate,’ he told him, and the old man locked the garden gate.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالسِّتِّ دُنْيَا طَلَعَتْ مِنْ بَابِ السِّرِّ فَلَمَّا رَأَيْتُهَا ظَنَنْتُ أَنَّ الْقَمَرَ قَدْ طَلَعَ مِنَ الْأُفُقِ وَأَضَاءَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-sitti dunyā ṭalaʿat min bābi al-sirri fa-lammā raʾaytuhā ẓanantu anna al-qamara qad ṭalaʿa mina al-ufuqi wa-aḍāʾa
sentences.l: And behold, the lady Dunyā came-out from the door of the secret; and when I saw her, I thought that the moon had risen from the horizon and shone.
sentences.i: And then the lady Dunyā came out through the private door; and when I saw her I thought the moon had risen over the horizon and shed its light.
sentences.n: ṭalaʿa is used twice: of Dunyā “coming out” and of the moon “rising”, the same verb, so the comparison is built into the words.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرْتُ لَهَا سَاعَةً زَمَانِيَّةً وَصِرْتُ مُشْتَاقًا إِلَيْهَا كَاشْتِيَاقِ الظَّمْأٰنِ إِلَى الْمَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓartu lahā sāʿatan zamāniyyatan wa-ṣirtu mushtāqan ilayhā ka-ishtiyāqi al-ẓamʾāni ilā al-māʾi
sentences.l: And I looked at her an hour of time, and I became longing for her like the longing of the thirsty-one for water.
sentences.i: I gazed at her for a full hour, and came to long for her as the thirsty long for water.
sentences.n: naẓartu lahā, “I looked at her”, with li- where Classical says ilā. sāʿatan zamāniyyatan, “an hour of time”, i.e. a full hour, a stock phrase of the later Nights. ka-ishtiyāqi, “like the longing”: ka- makes the comparison. al-ẓamʾān, “the thirsty one”, is spelled in the print with a hamza on the alif and no madda; the long ā is marked here with a small dagger alif.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ أَغْلَقَتِ الْبَابَ وَمَضَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda sāʿatin aghlaqati al-bāba wa-maḍat
sentences.l: And after an hour she shut the door and went-away.
sentences.i: After an hour she closed the door and was gone.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ خَرَجْتُ أَنَا مِنَ الْبُسْتَانِ وَطَلَبْتُ مَنْزِلِي
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika kharajtu anā mina al-bustāni wa-ṭalabtu manzilī
sentences.l: And at that I went-out, I, from the garden and sought my lodging.
sentences.i: Then I left the garden and made for my lodging.

sentences.t: وَعَرَفْتُ أَنِّي لَا أَصِلُ إِلَيْهَا وَلَا أَنَا مِنْ رِجَالِهَا خُصُوصًا وَأَنَا قَدْ صِرْتُ مِثْلَ الْمَرْأَةِ لَيْسَ لِي آلَةُ رِجَالٍ وَهِيَ بِنْتُ مَلِكٍ وَأَنَا رَجُلٌ تَاجِرٌ فَمِنْ أَيْنَ لِي وُصُولٌ إِلَى مِثْلِ هَذِهِ أَوْ غَيْرِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ʿaraftu annī lā aṣilu ilayhā wa-lā anā min rijālihā khuṣūṣan wa-anā qad ṣirtu mithla al-marʾati laysa lī ālatu rijālin wa-hiya bintu malikin wa-anā rajulun tājirun fa-min ayna lī wuṣūlun ilā mithli hādhihi aw ghayrihā
sentences.l: And I knew that I do not reach to her, nor am I of her men — especially and I have become like the woman, there is not to me the member of men; and she is a king’s daughter and I am a merchant man. So from where to me a reaching to the like of this one, or to another?
sentences.i: And I knew that I could never come to her, nor was I a man for her — least of all now that I had become like a woman, with no male member left to me. She is a king’s daughter and I a merchant: how should I ever come to such a one as she, or to any woman at all?
sentences.n: min rijālihā, “of her men”: not a match for her. ālatu rijālin, “the instrument of men”: his genitals, which the lady cut off in Night 126. khuṣūṣan wa-, “especially since”, a spoken turn. fa-min ayna lī, “whence to me?”: a rhetorical “how could I ever”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَجَهَّزَتْ أَصْحَابِي هَؤُلَاءِ تَجَهَّزْتُ أَنَا وَسَافَرْتُ مَعَهُمْ وَهُمْ قَاصِدُونَ هَذِهِ الْبَلْدَةَ حَتَّى إِذَا وَصَلْنَا إِلَى هَذَا الْمَكَانِ وَاجْتَمَعْنَا بِكَ وَسَأَلْتَنِى فَأَخْبَرْتُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā tajahhazat aṣḥābī hāʾulāʾi tajahhaztu anā wa-sāfartu maʿahum wa-hum qāṣidūna hādhihi al-baldata ḥattā idhā waṣalnā ilā hādhā al-makāni wa-ijtamaʿnā bika wa-saʾaltanī fa-akhbartuka
sentences.l: And when these my companions made-ready, I made-ready, I, and travelled with them, they heading for this town; until, when we reached this place and met with you and you asked me, I told you.
sentences.i: When these companions of mine made ready to leave, I made ready too and travelled with them, bound for this city; and so we came to this place and met you, and you asked me, and I told you.
sentences.n: ijtamaʿnā bika, “we met with you”: ijtamaʿa takes bi- for the person met. saʾaltanī, “you asked me”, spelled in the print with final ى.

sentences.t: وَهَذِهِ حِكَايَتِي وَمَا جَرَى لِي وَالسَّلَامُ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhihi ḥikāyatī wa-mā jarā lī wa-al-salāmu
sentences.l: And this is my story and what happened to me, and peace.
sentences.i: That is my story and all that befell me — and there it ends.”
sentences.n: wa-al-salām, “and peace”: the formula that closes a letter or a tale, “and that is all”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ اشْتَغَلَ بَالُهُ وَفِكْرُهُ بِحُبِّ السَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا وَحَارَ فِي أَمْرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa tāju al-mulūki dhālika al-kalāma ishtaghala bāluhu wa-fikruhu bi-ḥubbi al-sayyidati dunyā wa-ḥāra fī amrihi
sentences.l: And when Tāj al-Mulūk heard that speech, his mind and his thought became-busied with the love of the lady Dunyā, and he was perplexed in his affair.
sentences.i: When Tāj al-Mulūk heard this, his mind and his every thought were taken up with love for the lady Dunyā, and he did not know what to do.
sentences.n: ishtaghala bi-, “be occupied with”: bi- marks what fills the mind.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ نَهَضَ وَرَكِبَ جَوَادَهُ وَأَخَذَ عَزِيزًا مَعَهُ وَعَادَبِهِ إِلَى مَدِينَةِ أَبِيهِ وَأَفْرَدَ لِعَزِيزٍ دَارًا وَوَضَعَ لَهُ فِيهَا كُلَّ مَا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَأْكَلِ وَالْمَشْرَبِ وَالْمَلْبَسِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu nahaḍa wa-rakiba jawādahu wa-akhadha ʿazīzan maʿahu wa-ʿāda bihi ilā madīnati abīhi wa-afrada li-ʿazīzin dāran wa-waḍaʿa lahu fīhā kulla mā yaḥtāju ilayhi mina al-maʾkali wa-al-mashrabi wa-al-malbasi
sentences.l: Then he rose and mounted his steed and took ʿAzīz with him, and returned with him to the city of his father, and set-apart for ʿAzīz a house, and put for him in it all that he needs of food and drink and clothing.
sentences.i: Then he rose, mounted his horse, took ʿAzīz with him and brought him back to his father’s city. There he gave ʿAzīz a house of his own and furnished it with everything he could need in food, drink and clothing.
sentences.n: ʿāda bihi, “returned with him”, i.e. brought him back: ʿāda bi- is to bring back; run together in the print. afrada lahu dāran, “set apart a house for him”: gave him one to himself.

sentences.t: وَتَرَكَهُ وَمَضَى إِلَى قَصْرِهِ وَدُمُوعُهُ تَجْرِى عَلَى خُدُودِهِ لِأَنَّ السَّمَاعَ يَحُلُّ مَحَلَّ النَّظَرِ وَالِاجْتِمَاعِ
sentences.tr: wa-tarakahu wa-maḍā ilā qaṣrihi wa-dumūʿuhu tajrī ʿalā khudūdihi li-anna al-samāʿa yaḥullu maḥalla al-naẓari wa-al-ijtimāʿi
sentences.l: And he left him and went to his palace, his tears running on his cheeks; because hearing takes the place of looking and meeting.
sentences.i: Then he left him and went to his palace with tears running down his cheeks; for hearing of the beloved can take the place of seeing her and being with her.
sentences.n: The closing clause is a proverb-like saying in rhyme (samāʿ, ijtimāʿ): love can be kindled by report alone. tajrī, “run”, written with final ى in the print.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ تَاجُ الْمُلُوكِ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ حَتَّى دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ أَبُوهُ فَوَجَدَهُ مُتَغَيِّرَ اللَّوْنِ نَحِيفَ الْجِسْمِ بَاكِىَ الْعَيْنِ فَعَلِمَ أَنَّهُ مَهْمُومٌ لِأَمْرٍ نَزَلَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal tāju al-mulūki ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati ḥattā dakhala ʿalayhi abūhu fa-wajadahu mutaghayyira al-lawni naḥīfa al-jismi bākiya al-ʿayni fa-ʿalima annahu mahmūmun li-amrin nazala bihi
sentences.l: And Tāj al-Mulūk did not cease in that state until his father came-in on him and found him changed of colour, thin of body, weeping of eye; and he knew that he was grieved for a matter that had come-down upon him.
sentences.i: Tāj al-Mulūk stayed in that state until his father came in to him and found him pale, wasted and tearful, and knew that he was troubled by something that had befallen him.
sentences.n: mutaghayyira al-lawni, naḥīfa al-jismi, bākiya al-ʿayni: three “improper” construct phrases, adjective plus noun, “changed of colour, thin of body, weeping of eye”. bākī is written with final ى in the print. nazala bihi, “came down on him”: bi- marks the one it befalls.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي أَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ حَالِكَ وَمَا الَّذِي جَرَى لَكَ حَتَّى تَغَيَّرَ لَوْنُكَ وَنَحَلَ جِسْمُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā waladī akhbirnī ʿan ḥālika wa-mā alladhī jarā laka ḥattā taghayyara lawnuka wa-naḥala jismuka
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my son, tell me about your state, and what is it that has happened to you, so that your colour has changed and your body grown-thin?
sentences.i: He said to him: “My son, tell me how you are, and what has happened to you, that your colour has changed and your body wasted away.”

sentences.t: فَأَعَادَ لَهُ جَمِيعَ مَا جَرَى لَهُ وَمَا سَمِعَهُ مِنْ قِصَّةِ عَزِيزٍ وَقِصَّةِ السَّيِّدَةِ دُنْيَا وَأَنَّهُ عَشِقَهَا عَلَى السَّمَاعِ وَلَمْ يَنْظُرْهَا بِالْعَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-aʿāda lahu jamīʿa mā jarā lahu wa-mā samiʿahu min qiṣṣati ʿazīzin wa-qiṣṣati al-sayyidati dunyā wa-annahu ʿashiqahā ʿalā al-samāʿi wa-lam yanẓurhā bi-al-ʿayni
sentences.l: And he repeated to him all that had happened to him, and what he had heard of the story of ʿAzīz and the story of the lady Dunyā, and that he had fallen-in-love-with her upon hearing and had not looked at her with the eye.
sentences.i: So he told him again all that had befallen him, and what he had heard of ʿAzīz’s story and the lady Dunyā’s, and how he had fallen in love with her by hearsay without ever setting eyes on her.
sentences.n: The print has دينا, a misprint for دنيا (Dunyā), corrected here. ʿalā al-samāʿi, “upon hearing”, i.e. by report. bi-al-ʿayni, “with the eye”: bi- of the means. aʿāda lahu, “repeated to him”: the storyteller does not retell the story a second time.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا وَلَدِي إِنَّهَا بِنْتُ مَلِكٍ وَبِلَادُهُ بَعِيدَةٌ عَنَّا فَدَعْ عَنْكَ هَذَا وَادْخُلْ إِلَى قَصْرِ أُمِّكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā waladī innahā bintu malikin wa-bilāduhu baʿīdatun ʿannā fa-daʿ ʿanka hādhā wa-udkhul ilā qaṣri ummika
sentences.l: And he said: O my son, she is the daughter of a king and his lands are far from us; so leave this from you, and go-in to the palace of your mother.
sentences.i: He said: “My son, she is a king’s daughter and her father’s lands are far from us. Put this out of your mind, and go in to your mother’s palace.”
sentences.n: daʿ ʿanka hādhā, “leave this from you”: put it aside, give it up.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
